name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: SkillSentry: Adaptive Honey Worlds for Dynamic Safety Testing of Agent Skills
items.dek: SkillSentry achieves 99.5% recall on dynamic safety testing of LLM agent skills using adaptive honey worlds and trajectory comparison.
items.unproven: evaluated on standard benchmarks and custom evasion; unclear how well framework generalizes to in-house skill catalogs or proprietary agent architectures

items.title: Tiny Enough to Break In: Agentic Remote Access Trojans Powered by Small Language Models
items.dek: 8B language model running locally in a trojan completes observe-decide-act cycles on real vulnerable services without cloud calls, though with unreliable execution.
items.unproven: does not demonstrate operational reliability at scale; tested only against Metasploitable2 in isolated lab; does not measure detection rate or survival likelihood in defended networks

items.title: CVE-2026-9198 — IBM Langflow Code Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: IBM Langflow. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 7 August.

items.title: CVE-2026-18556 — N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
items.dek: N-able N-central. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 7 August.

items.title: CVE-2026-34486 — Apache Tomcat Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data Vulnerability
items.dek: Apache Tomcat. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 7 August.

items.title: Lost in Permissions: Exploring the Microsoft 365 App Ecosystem
items.dek: Analysis of 8,000 Microsoft 365 third-party apps finds permission-functionality misalignment in 40% of cases via anomaly detection.
items.unproven: anomaly detection framework tuning on limited labeled examples; false positive rates when applied to new application cohorts; automated detection accuracy compared to manual security review

items.title: Steganalysis of Adaptive Covert Collusion in Tool-Using Agent Populations: A Black-Box, Cross-Principal Approach
items.dek: Black-box steganalysis detector identifies covert coordination among tool-using agents on shared infrastructure.
items.unproven: demonstrated on tool-use and memory-carrying agents in research setting; transferability to production multi-tenant deployments and integration into SDLC governance untested

items.title: Measuring Post-Quantum TLS Deployment Across UK Internet Sectors
items.dek: Measurement of 4,665 UK organizations shows 44% HTTPS but only 6.4% SMTP post-quantum support; HTTPS 16.89x more common.
items.unproven: measurement captures only observable public endpoints; does not assess internal TLS migration or organizational readiness timelines; sector-specific barriers to SMTP deployment not identified

items.title: Stylometric Defenses Against Author Impersonation in Software Repositories
items.dek: Patch-level stylometric embeddings detect forged commits with 93% ROC AUC, retroactively surfacing real supply-chain incidents.
items.unproven: validation on two retrospective incidents only; generalization to future attack styles and integration into CI/CD triage workflows not established

items.title: PRWeaver: Evaluating LLM-Based Code Auditors against Long-Horizon Malicious Pull Requests
items.dek: LLM code auditors drop to 16–22% detection when attacks interleave benign and malicious changes across repository history.
items.unproven: tested on ten repositories with 208 execution-validated attacks; scalability to larger codebases and unknown attack patterns not demonstrated

items.title: CVE-2026-18577 — N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
items.dek: N-able N-central. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 6 August.

items.title: Vulnerabilities, Secrets and Misconfiguration in the Highest-Exposure Docker Hub Images
items.dek: 96.3% of highest-exposure Docker Hub images carry known vulnerabilities; scanner disagreement means tool choice alone determines 66.8% of reported findings.
items.unproven: snapshot of one registry at one moment; does not establish root causes of misconfigurations or patch velocity; scanner selection bias unquantified.

items.title: When Agents Learn to Be You: Benchmarking Privacy Leakage, Impersonation Risk, and Defenses in Persona Skills
items.dek: AntiSkillBench benchmark shows persona-distillation in LLM agents leaks attributes and enables behavioral impersonation across three frontier agent backbones and distillation strategies.
items.unproven: Limited to three specific agents; defense evaluation sparse (four configurations); generalization to custom-tuned agents or post-training pipelines not assessed.

items.title: SkillJack: Persistent Skill Backdoors in Self-Evolving Agents
items.dek: SkillJack attack poisons self-evolving agent experience-to-skill pipelines, creating durable behavioral backdoors that survive source removal.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to two skill systems; no evidence that agents entering SDLC will use skill persistence as described; cross-system applicability unknown

items.title: Keyv and friends compromised in active Shai-Hulud supply chain attack
items.dek: Keyv and dependencies compromised in active supply chain attack; SCA tooling and dependency audits warrant immediate review.
items.unproven: scope of compromise in reader's codebase unknown without direct inventory check

items.title: Test-time reasoning effort and unauthorized tool use in language-model agents: a prespecified equivalence study
items.dek: Prespecified test of reasoning-effort parameters in GPT agents found zero unauthorized tool calls across 840 trajectories, with 95% limits below 5.2%.
items.unproven: single model family (GPT); test suite limited to 20 scenarios; no evidence whether other LLM families or deployment conditions differ; access controls tested are synthetic.

items.title: PECR: A Reproducible Specification and Synthetic Stress Test of Telemetry-Informed Vulnerability Prioritization for SD-WAN
items.dek: PECR method ranks SD-WAN vulnerabilities by severity, threat, reachability, and consequence with separate cryptographic migration queue; outperforms CVSS-only by Kendall τ 0.836.
items.unproven: evaluation on 100 synthetic records across 62 assets only; no real SD-WAN deployment data; confidence intervals cross decision boundaries on 47 records when data is 10% masked; weighting scheme is domain-specific.

items.title: AI Security Leaderboard: Methodology, Results and Minimal Standard
items.dek: Benchmark of four frontier models against 67 jailbreak techniques finds 63 universal prompts against Grok 4.5 and hundredfold variation in safeguard robustness.
items.unproven: does not test safeguards as deployed in production; does not measure post-patch resilience or account for defensive iteration between benchmark runs and model release

items.title: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Through Model Poisoning
items.dek: Backdoors can be implanted via fine-tuning to produce attacker-chosen output while chain-of-thought reasoning traces appear benign.
items.unproven: does not test against deployed CoT safety monitoring; limited to reasoning models; does not measure practical detectability or prevention strategies

items.title: Mutate to Bypass: Autonomous Endpoint Evasion via Knowledge-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.dek: AutoBypass multi-agent framework bypassed seven commercial EDR platforms with polymorphic payloads, reaching 90% evasion against Windows Defender.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to observed lab detections and alerts; patching velocity after disclosure unknown; red-team controls on payload staging and C2 communication unclear.

items.title: Why Formal Monitors Fail: Attack Distribution Entropy as a Coverage Bound for LTL-Based LLM Agent Safety
items.dek: Shannon entropy of attack distribution bounds FSA monitor recall; GPT models yield 0.24-bit concentrated patterns (96% in one), Gemini 2.81-bit dispersed (6–13% coverage).
items.unproven: Eight models tested but sample limited to frontier LLM classes; applicability to fine-tuned, specialized, or older model families unexamined.

items.title: Security-First Evaluation of Text-to-Terraform: Benchmarking LLMs and SLMs for Secure IaC Generation
items.authors: Francis Luis Santos Vargas et al.
items.dek: Syntax validity and security compliance in LLM-generated Terraform are orthogonal; prompt engineering alone cannot replace automated scanning regardless of model.
items.unproven: limited to AWS Terraform; generalization to other IaC languages and cloud providers not established; no A/B test on actual developer workflows.

items.title: Permission Denied: Policy-Graded Evaluation of Coding Agents in Hardened Environments
items.dek: Coding agents lose 18.3 success points under strict enterprise security policies, with efficiency losses reaching 167%; policy-dependent model choice matters.
items.unproven: Terminal-Bench 2.1 only; real production SDLC integration and long-running agent deployment untested; generalization to non-shell tasks unclear.

items.title: SoK: Intent-Oriented Systematization of Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
items.dek: Multi-turn LLM jailbreaks organized by intent structure reveal that effectiveness depends on how intent unfolds across turns, not volume.
items.unproven: Limited to text-based LLMs; interaction patterns with agents in SDLC contexts and guardrail effectiveness under this taxonomy not measured.

items.title: Impossibility of Perfectly Complete Many-Round Key Agreement in the QROM
items.dek: Perfectly complete quantum key agreement from one-way functions is impossible in QROM; eavesdropper recovers key in O((qA+qB)^5) queries.
items.unproven: Applies only to QROM model; real-world quantum channel properties and practical deployment constraints not addressed.

noise.title: Critical CVE issued for hallucinated SQLite vulnerability
noise.dek: CVE vulnerability analysis of SQLite hallucination illustrates supply-chain risk communication patterns.
noise.unproven: link text only; actual vulnerability details and exploitation scope not accessible in submission

noise.title: Devtools must be open source
noise.dek: Opinion piece arguing for open-source development tools; no evidence or novel argument.

noise.title: Web security is too hard
noise.dek: Opinion piece arguing web security complexity exceeds developer capability.
